agents-md-complete-guide.title: AGENTS.md Complete Guide — Make Every Coding Agent Follow Your Repo Rules
agents-md-complete-guide.description: How to write AGENTS.md (and related instruction files) so Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, and others respect your architecture, tests, and safety rules. Includes OS-specific pitfalls, permission boundaries, and a loop to prove the agent is actually reading it.

beware-claude-code-disallowedtools-not-i.title: Beware: Claude Code's disallowedTools Don't Reach Subagents — Your Deny List Is a Parent-Only Guard
beware-claude-code-disallowedtools-not-i.description: A reproducible Claude Code bug shows that tools you explicitly deny in settings are NOT inherited by subagents spawned through the Agent tool. If your safety model assumes a global deny list, subagents can run the very tools you blocked.

beware-claude-code-edit-tool-false-strin.title: Beware: Claude Code's Edit Tool Rejects Strings That Are in the File
beware-claude-code-edit-tool-false-strin.description: A confirmed, reproducible Claude Code bug (issue #78076) makes the Edit tool return \"String not found in file\" for multi-line text that is byte-identical to the current file. It's a file-state desync that fails real edits and teaches agents a wrong model of reality.

beware-claude-code-permissions-deny-abso.title: Beware: Claude Code's permissions.deny Silently Fails on Absolute Paths — Your Credential Guard May Be a No-Op
beware-claude-code-permissions-deny-abso.description: A documented Claude Code behavior means a permissions.deny rule written with a single leading slash resolves as project-relative and matches nothing — with no warning. If you hardened your project against reads of ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or .env this way, the guard may be doing nothing.

beware-coding-agent-sandbox-leaks-own-cr.title: Beware: Your Coding Agent's Sandbox Was Leaking Its Own Credentials to Spawned Commands
beware-coding-agent-sandbox-leaks-own-cr.description: A coordinated wave of security fixes across Gitlawb/zero and Goose shows the 'sandbox' you trusted was handing provider API keys, OAuth tokens, MCP OAuth tokens, and daemon bearer tokens to every command it spawned. Here's who's exposed, the real PRs, and how to contain it.

beware-oh-my-pi-subagent-write-root-esca.title: Beware: Oh-My-Pi Subagents Can Write Into Your Protected Parent Checkout (Write-Root Not Enforced)
beware-oh-my-pi-subagent-write-root-esca.description: A verified oh-my-pi bug shows non-isolated subagents inherit the parent cwd with no enforced write boundary, so edit/write/ast_edit calls can silently land in your main checkout. Here's who's affected, the real incident, and how to contain it.

what-devs-say-claude-code-vs-cursor.description: Community patterns for Claude Code vs Cursor—IDE speed versus terminal depth, hybrid stacks, failure modes, and how to turn anecdotes into a team default.

beware-coding-agents-trip-edr-rules-like.title: Beware: Your Coding Agent Trips the Same EDR Rules Built to Catch Attackers
beware-coding-agents-trip-edr-rules-like.description: Sophos telemetry from June 2026 shows Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex setting off credential-access, LOLBin, and persistence rules on Windows endpoints — because to a behavioral engine, benign agent work is indistinguishable from an intrusion. Here's what fired, why allowlisting is the wrong fix, and how to scope it safely.

beware-claude-code-approval-preview-unic.title: Beware: Claude Code's Approval Previews Could Be Spoofed With Invisible Unicode
beware-claude-code-approval-preview-unic.description: Claude Code 2.1.211 (July 15) quietly patched a flaw where permission-approval previews sent to chat channels didn't strip bidirectional-override, zero-width, and look-alike quote characters. A tool input could render as one command in the approval card and execute as another. Here's how the spoof works and how to approve safely.

beware-claude-code-plan-mode-permission-.title: Beware: Claude Code v2.1.212 Patched Three Silent Safety Holes — Plan-Mode Bypass, Worktree Escape, SIGTERM Orphans
beware-claude-code-plan-mode-permission-.description: Claude Code v2.1.212 (July 17, 2026) closed three safety boundaries at once: a plan-mode hole that ran touch and rm with no prompt, a worktree symlink escape that could write files outside the repo, and a SIGTERM that orphaned the process tree. Here is what changed, who was exposed, and how to verify your install.

coding-agents-build-circuit-breakers-202.title: The Week Coding Agents Learned to Pull Their Own Plug
coding-agents-build-circuit-breakers-202.description: In one week Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex each shipped a circuit breaker: caps on runaway loops, default-off nested subagents, and harder dangerous-command guards. Here's what that signals about where autonomous coding agents are heading.

beware-codex-multiagentv2-encrypts-subag.title: Beware: Codex MultiAgentV2 Encrypts What Your Parent Agent Told Its Subagents — And You Can't Read It Locally
beware-codex-multiagentv2-encrypts-subag.description: On GPT-5.6-Sol and Terra, Codex CLI 0.144.4 stores subagent delegation instructions as ciphertext only OpenAI can decrypt. You can see that a handoff happened, not what was delegated. Here's the blast radius and how to keep your workflows auditable.

beware-gitlawb-zero-mcp-trust-boundary-v.title: Beware: Gitlawb Zero v0.4.0 Closed a Hole Where a Cloned Repo Could Re-Enable the MCP Servers You Disabled
beware-gitlawb-zero-mcp-trust-boundary-v.description: Gitlawb Zero v0.4.0 (July 17, 2026) shipped a quiet but important security fix: a project-level config could previously override a user's disabled MCP server. For anyone who treats MCP as a security boundary, this is the kind of trust gap worth understanding before your next git clone.

beware-claude-code-auto-mode-overrides-h.title: Beware: Claude Code's Auto Mode Could Silently Override Your PreToolUse Hook 'Ask' Guard — Your Hook Floor Was a No-Op
beware-claude-code-auto-mode-overrides-h.description: Claude Code v2.1.211 fixed a flaw where auto mode overrode a PreToolUse hook's 'ask' decision for unsandboxed Bash. If you configured a hook to stop and prompt you before risky commands, auto mode could bypass it and proceed. Here is what it means for your security workflow.

beware-claude-code-v2-1-214-permission-f.title: Beware: Claude Code v2.1.214 Quietly Closed Six Permission Holes at Once — The Fail-Open Pattern Operators Should Audit
beware-claude-code-v2-1-214-permission-f.description: Claude Code v2.1.214 (July 18, 2026) patched a cluster of permission fail-open behaviors: over-broad dir/** allow rules, Windows PowerShell 5.1 bypass, file-descriptor redirects, 10k-char commands, zsh subscript parsing, help/man with unsafe options, and unprompted docker daemon-redirect flags. Here is what changed, which workflows break, and how to verify your install.

grok-build-xai-coding-agent-17k-stars.title: Grok Build: xAI's Coding Agent Hits 17K Stars in One Week
grok-build-xai-coding-agent-17k-stars.description: xAI just dropped Grok Build — a terminal-based coding agent that's already the most starred AI coding tool on GitHub. Here's what it does differently.

openclaw-2026-7-2-control-plane.title: OpenClaw 2026.7.2 Quietly Becomes a Control Plane for Other Coding Agents
openclaw-2026-7-2-control-plane.description: OpenClaw's 2026.7.2 beta can resume OpenCode and Pi sessions, open Codex and Claude catalog sessions in a terminal on their owning host, and run its UI on cloud workers. Here's what that control-plane move signals about agent orchestration.

beware-cve-2026-55607-claude-code-worktr.title: Beware: Claude Code CVE-2026-55607 — A Malicious Repo Can Escape the Sandbox and Execute Code on Your Machine
beware-cve-2026-55607-claude-code-worktr.description: CVE-2026-55607 is an 8.8-severity sandbox escape in Claude Code that lets a malicious repository chain git worktree naming, symlink tricks, and shell startup files into full host execution. Fixed in v2.1.163. Here's what happened, who was exposed, and how to verify.

ai-coding-agents-unfiltered-truth-develo.title: AI Coding Agents: The Unfiltered Truth From Developers Who Use Them All Day
ai-coding-agents-unfiltered-truth-develo.description: We talked to dozens of developers living inside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and open-source agents. The consensus is sharper than the marketing — and it is not what you'd expect.

klaatcode-open-source-coding-agent-termi.title: KlaatCode: The Open-Source Coding Agent That Wants to Beat Claude Code
klaatcode-open-source-coding-agent-termi.description: KlaatCode is a new open-source terminal coding agent claiming Claude Code-grade accuracy. We tested it against the real thing.

claude-code-end-conversation-fire-user.title: Claude Code Now Has a \"Fire the User\" Button — What EndConversation Means for Coding Workflows
claude-code-end-conversation-fire-user.description: Claude Code v2.1.214 introduced EndConversation, a tool that lets the agent terminate your session if it considers you abusive or a jailbreak attempt. Here is what it does, why Anthropic added it, and how it changes the operator-agent power dynamic.
